# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 18, 2026
**Re:** Logith Auto Auctions, LLC / Draibav Systems, Inc.: LaneCast license issues review before the Ostrander closing
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Summary and priorities

I reviewed all seven documents in the folder:

1. Software License Agreement, effective June 16, 2025 (the "**License Agreement**" or "**LA**")
2. Service Level Schedule ("**SLS**")
3. Order Form No. LC-2025-0614 ("**OF**")
4. Amendment No. 1, dated May 29, 2026 ("**Amendment**")
5. Term sheet, dated May 9, 2025
6. Mutual NDA, dated April 14, 2025
7. Draibav's certificate of insurance, dated June 2, 2026

I found six issues. Two of them will be triggered by the Logith Holdings–Ostrander closing, which Amendment Recital B says is expected in Q4 2026. That makes them urgent now.

**How the documents fit together.** Under LA §2.3, conflicts are resolved in this order:

- Amendments
- then the **Order Form**
- then the body of the License Agreement
- then the SLS

So **the Order Form prevails over the body of the License Agreement**, and the Amendment prevails over both. The integration clause in LA §16.2 supersedes the term sheet. Where the signed documents depart from the term sheet, the term sheet helps us in negotiation but gives us no contractual rights.

**Dollar figures.** Monthly Subscription Fees are $78,000 (OF §6.1).
- The 12-month liability cap is therefore about **$936,000**.
- Accelerated fees for the rest of the initial term, from a Q4 2026 closing to June 30, 2030, come to about **$3.3–3.4 million**.

| Priority | Issue | Location | Exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 – Urgent (before closing)** | Change-of-control consent not obtained | LA §15.2; Amendment Recital B | Incurable material breach at closing; termination plus acceleration of about $3.3M+ |
| **2 – Urgent (before closing)** | Overbroad exclusivity will reach Ostrander | LA §3.4; Term Sheet §4 | Breach at closing because of Ostrander's incumbent auction software |
| **3 – Urgent (live dispute)** | Chronic Failure termination notice sent 4 days late | SLS §5.2; Amendment Recital C, §6 | Exit right at risk; stated effective date (Oct. 31, 2026) has already passed |
| **4 – High** | Narrow "Licensee Data" definition lets Draibav commercialize bidder and transaction data | OF §4.1; LA §§1.9, 7.4, 2.3 | Loss of control over core competitive data |
| **5 – High** | Data-breach liability now capped | LA §10.4(b); Amendment §3 | Data breach capped at about $936K |
| **6 – Medium (long-dated, fix now)** | 60-month auto-renewal with a narrow opt-out window | LA §12.2; OF §2.2 | Locked in until 2035 if the window is missed |

Issues 1–3 should be handled together in one negotiation with Draibav. Draibav's consent to the merger is our most valuable leverage point, and its counterparty position on the termination notice is its main leverage. Issues 4–6 should go into the same amendment.

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: The Ostrander merger requires Draibav's prior written consent, and no consent has been obtained

**Location:** LA §15.2 (Change of Control); LA §12.5; Amendment Recital B and §7.2.

**What the documents say:**
- **LA §15.2.** "Any direct or indirect change of control of Licensee … including any such transaction involving any entity that directly or indirectly controls Licensee" is deemed an assignment "requiring the prior written consent of Licensor." A change of control without consent:
  - is "a material breach … that is not capable of cure"; and
  - lets Draibav terminate on notice, which triggers LA §12.5.
- **LA §12.5.** On such a termination, all Subscription Fees for the rest of the then-current term become immediately due.
- **LA §15.1.** The "not unreasonably withheld" standard in §15.1 does **not** apply to the §15.2 consent, so Draibav has discretion.
- **Amendment Recital B.** Logith Holdings, Inc., Logith's parent, has signed an **Agreement and Plan of Merger dated April 20, 2026 with Ostrander Remarketing Partners, L.P.**, with closing expected in Q4 2026. That merger is an indirect change of control of Logith squarely within §15.2.

**Why it matters:**
- **The Amendment does not supply consent.** It only *recites* that Logith informed Draibav of the merger. It contains no consent language. Amendment §7.2 and LA §16.4 also provide that nothing in the Amendment waives any provision, and that a waiver must be in writing and signed.
- **Knowledge is not consent.** Draibav's knowledge of the deal, even when acknowledged in a signed amendment, is not the "prior written consent" §15.2 requires. Delaware courts generally enforce express anti-assignment and consent provisions as written.
- **Consequences of closing without consent:**
  - Draibav could terminate immediately with no cure period.
  - Draibav could claim about $3.3M+ in accelerated fees.
  - Logith would lose its six-site auction platform at a sensitive integration moment.
  - Transition assistance under LA §12.7 is unavailable when Draibav terminates under §12.3. A §15.2 termination imports §12.5, and Draibav will argue the same exclusion applies.
- **Deal-level effects.** This likely bears on Holdings' representations and closing conditions under the merger agreement (third-party consents and material contracts). The M&A team should be looped in.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Before closing**, obtain a signed written consent from Draibav. Ideally put it in an Amendment No. 2 that expressly:
   - consents to the Holdings–Ostrander merger; and
   - waives termination and acceleration under §§15.2 and 12.5 for that transaction.
2. Negotiate a permanent fix to §15.2 at the same time:
   - a "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed" standard;
   - a carve-out for changes of control at the parent level or to a non-competitor of Draibav; and
   - deletion of "not capable of cure."
3. Confirm with deal counsel whether the merger agreement makes this consent a closing condition or a covenant. If timing is tight, consider whether closing can be conditioned on the consent.
4. Package this consent with Issues 2 and 3 below. Draibav will want something for its consent, and these are the points we need to win.

---

### Issue 2: The exclusivity clause binds all Affiliates across the US and Canada and goes well beyond the term sheet

**Location:** LA §3.4 (Exclusivity); LA §1.1 ("Affiliate"); compare Term Sheet §4.

**What the documents say:**
- **LA §3.4.** Logith "shall cause its Affiliates not to … license, use, develop or procure, anywhere in the United States or Canada, any online, simulcast or mobile vehicle auction software, bidding software or condition reporting software other than the Platform." It covers both third-party and internally developed software.
- **Term Sheet §4.1.** Limited exclusivity to "simulcast bidding software at the six Licensed Sites only."
- **Term Sheet §4.2.** Expressly preserved Logith's and its affiliates' freedom for "any other software or any other facility."
- **One-way deal.** The license Draibav grants Logith is **non-exclusive** (LA §3.1), so Logith gets nothing in return for this restriction.

**Why it matters:**
- **The clause covers far more than agreed:**
  - It reaches every auction function: online, mobile, bidding and condition reporting, not just simulcast.
  - It applies everywhere in the US and Canada, not just the six sites.
  - It binds every Affiliate, not just Logith.
- **New sites are captured.** Any site Logith adds or acquires must use LaneCast at Draibav's then-current pricing (LA §3.3).
- **The Ostrander problem.** "Affiliate" (LA §1.1) includes entities under common control. After closing, Ostrander and its existing auction facilities become Affiliates of Logith. Their incumbent simulcast, online and condition-reporting tools would put Logith in breach of §3.4 **on the closing date**. Draibav could then:
  - terminate for material breach (LA §12.3(a));
  - accelerate fees (LA §12.5); and
  - use the clause to force Ostrander's whole platform onto LaneCast.
- **Integration risk.** The clause also restricts the combined company's technology integration choices through June 2030 and any renewal term.
- **Term sheet is not enforceable here.** LA §16.2 supersedes it. The clause may face enforceability arguments as an unreasonable restraint, but we should not rely on litigation.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Narrow §3.4 to the term-sheet deal: simulcast bidding software at the six Licensed Sites only. Add an express statement, mirroring Term Sheet §4.2, that nothing restricts other software or other facilities.
2. Expressly exclude Ostrander and any other entity that becomes an Affiliate through acquisition or change of control, together with their existing and future facilities.
3. If Draibav will not narrow the clause before closing, at minimum obtain a written waiver of §3.4 covering Ostrander and its affiliates. Make it part of the change-of-control consent package (Issue 1).
4. Advise the client and Ostrander's team not to put any Ostrander system in use at, or bring any Ostrander system to, Logith sites until this is resolved.

---

### Issue 3: The Chronic Failure termination notice was four days late, and the exit right is in dispute

**Location:** SLS §§5.1–5.2; Amendment Recital C and §6; LA §§12.4, 16.4.

**What the documents say:**
- **SLS §5.1.** A Chronic Failure occurs when Monthly Availability is below 99.0% in three months within any rolling six-month period.
- **Amendment Recital C.** Availability was 98.1% (January 2026), 97.6% (February 2026) and 98.4% (March 2026). That is a Chronic Failure.
- **SLS §5.2.** Notice must be given "within thirty (30) days after the end of the third affected month." The third month ended March 31, 2026, so **the window closed April 30, 2026.**
- **The notice.** Logith's Termination Notice is **dated May 4, 2026, four days late**. It stated an effective date of October 31, 2026.
- **Draibav's position.** Draibav disputed the notice by letter dated May 11, 2026.
- **Amendment §6.** Each side reserves all rights, expressly including "whether the Termination Notice was timely and effective." Signing the Amendment is neither acceptance nor rejection of the notice.

**Why it matters:**
- **Strict enforcement risk.** Contractual notice deadlines for termination rights are generally enforced strictly, and the License Agreement has a strong no-waiver clause (LA §16.4; Amendment §7.2). Draibav therefore has a credible argument that the notice was ineffective. If so, the Agreement continues through June 30, 2030.
- **The stated effective date has already passed.** If Logith has stopped paying, or has moved off LaneCast, in reliance on the notice and the notice is held ineffective, Draibav could claim:
  - non-payment and material breach;
  - termination under LA §12.3; and
  - acceleration under LA §12.5.
  This turns a lost exit right into roughly a $3.3M claim.
- **What we keep if the notice holds.** If the notice is effective, Logith exits without early termination fees (SLS §5.2; LA §12.4) and keeps refund and transition rights (LA §§12.6(c), 12.7).
- **Logith's position is preserved but not secure.** The reservation in Amendment §6 keeps Logith's arguments alive, for example:
  - substantial compliance and lack of prejudice to Draibav;
  - waiver or estoppel arising from Draibav's conduct; and
  - disproportionate forfeiture.
  These arguments run against the express no-waiver language.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Confirm the current operational and payment status immediately.** Has Logith continued to pay and use LaneCast after October 31, 2026? If it has not, assess our breach exposure now and consider a without-prejudice standstill or interim payment arrangement with Draibav.
2. **Look for a fresh termination right.**
   - Pull Draibav's SLS §2.4 monthly reports for April through October 2026. Any month below 99.0% within a rolling six-month window that includes two other sub-99.0% months creates a **new** Chronic Failure with a new 30-day window. The corrective action plan under Amendment §4 suggests the problems may not have been fixed.
   - Check the SLS §5.3 Severity 1 termination trigger as well.
   - Calendar every future window from the date each monthly report is received.
3. **Keep the litigation position alive.** Continue to rely on Amendment §6 to argue substantial compliance and waiver or estoppel.
4. **Use the dispute in the consent negotiation.** Negotiate a resolution as part of the consent package, either:
   - Draibav accepts the notice, or agrees a fresh no-fee exit right (by site or in whole); or
   - Draibav gives a fee concession in exchange for Logith withdrawing the notice.
5. **Going forward**, amend SLS §5.2 so that the window runs from Logith's receipt of the monthly report showing the third failure, and lengthen it to 60 days.

---

### Issue 4: The Order Form's narrow "Licensee Data" definition controls and opens bidder and transaction data to Draibav's commercial use

**Location:** OF §4.1; LA §§1.9, 2.3, 7.1–7.4; LA §8.1 (as amended); Amendment §3 (Section 8A).

**What the documents say:**
- **LA §1.9 (broad definition).** "Licensee Data" includes all data submitted to, collected by or generated by the Platform in connection with Logith's auctions, specifically:
  - Bidder and Consignor registration data;
  - bid histories;
  - hammer, floor and reserve prices;
  - condition reports;
  - transaction data; and
  - derivatives of all of these.
- **OF §4.1 (narrow definition).** Redefines "Licensee Data" as data "**uploaded to the Platform by Licensee's Authorized Users**." Authorized Users are Logith's own employees, contractors and agents (LA §1.2). Bidders and Consignors are not Authorized Users.
- **Which definition controls.** Under LA §2.3 the **Order Form prevails** over the body of the Agreement, so the narrow definition controls.
- **LA §7.4.** Draibav may "collect, use, aggregate, analyze and commercialize" Platform data "**other than Licensee Data**," including "data generated by the Platform." It may sell "analytics products, market reports and **market pricing benchmarks** to third parties."

**Why it matters:**
- **Core data falls outside Logith's protection.** Under the narrow definition, the following fall outside "Licensee Data":
  - bidder and consignor registration data entered by bidders and consignors;
  - bids and proxy bids;
  - hammer prices; and
  - Platform-generated transaction data.
  Logith therefore loses ownership of that data (LA §7.1), its return (LA §7.3) and the use limitation (LA §7.2).
- **Draibav can sell it.** Draibav can commercialize this data under LA §7.4, including by selling pricing benchmarks built from Logith's sale results to competing auctions. This reverses Term Sheet §7, under which Logith owned all of this data and Draibav could use only anonymized operational data.
- **Knock-on effects:**
  - The new Section 8A security obligations protect only "Licensee Data," so bidder and consignor personal and financial data may fall outside the strengthened security regime.
  - Licensee Data is carved out of "Confidential Information" (LA §8.1), so confidentiality does not backstop it either.
  - This complicates Logith's own compliance under GLBA and state and Canadian privacy laws (LA §7.5).

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend the Order Form to delete OF §4.1, or conform it to LA §1.9. Add an express provision that LA §1.9 controls notwithstanding LA §2.3.
2. Tighten LA §7.4 so that Draibav may use only aggregated, de-identified operational data that cannot be associated with Logith, any Licensed Site, Bidder or Consignor. Bar sales of pricing benchmarks derived from Logith data, consistent with Term Sheet §7.2.
3. Ask Draibav to confirm in writing whether it has used or sold any Logith bidder or sale data under §7.4 to date.

---

### Issue 5: Amendment No. 1 moved data security into Section 8A, so data-breach liability is now capped

**Location:** LA §§10.3, 10.4(b); Amendment §§2, 3; LA §§8.1, 9.

**What the documents say:**
- **LA §10.3.** Caps each party's liability at fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, about **$936,000**.
- **LA §10.4(b).** Removes the cap for "a Party's **breach of Section 8**."
- **Original Section 8.** Data-security, audit, incident-notification and incident-response obligations sat in LA §§8.4–8.7.
- **Amendment §3.** Deletes "**Sections 8.4 through 8.7**" and inserts a "**new Section 8A**" with stronger standards (ISO 27001/NIST, MFA, 48-hour notice, expanded cost reimbursement).
- **What the Amendment did not change.** It amended §8.1 (Amendment §2) and §12.8 (Amendment §5) to refer to 8A, but it did **not** amend §10.4(b). Amendments rank first under LA §2.3, and Amendment §7.1 ratifies everything not expressly amended.

**Why it matters:**
- **The carve-out no longer reaches data breaches.** A breach of Draibav's data-security obligations is now a breach of Section 8A, not "Section 8." It therefore falls within the 12-month cap. The inconsistent cross-referencing makes this worse: the parties updated §§8.1 and 12.8 to refer to 8A, which lets Draibav argue the omission from §10.4(b) was deliberate.
- **No other route to uncapped recovery.** Licensee Data is excluded from "Confidential Information" (LA §8.1), so the remaining §8 confidentiality obligations do not cover it. The LA §9 indemnity covers only IP infringement.
- **Practical consequence.** A breach exposing Logith's bidder, dealer and payment data, including notification, forensics, credit monitoring, regulatory and third-party claims, would be capped at about $936K. This defeats the term sheet's agreed carve-out for "breach of confidentiality and data security obligations" (Term Sheet §8.2).
- **Insurance does not solve it.** Draibav carries $5M of cyber cover (see the COI below), but the contractual cap limits what Logith can recover regardless of the insurance.
- **The "stronger" amendment weakened Logith's position.** Logith received better security standards and lost meaningful recourse when those standards are breached.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend LA §10.4(b) to read "a Party's breach of Section 8 or Section 8A." Better, refer to "confidentiality, data security or data protection obligations, including Sections 7.5, 8 and 8A."
2. If Draibav insists on some limit, the fallback is a separate "super-cap" for data breaches (for example, the greater of 3x annual fees or $5M, matching Draibav's cyber limits). Keep uncapped treatment for gross negligence and willful misconduct (LA §10.4(c)).
3. Make clear that Section 8A costs (notification, forensics, credit monitoring) are direct damages and not excluded by LA §10.1.

---

### Issue 6: Automatic 60-month renewals with a single 30-day opt-out window

**Location:** LA §12.2; OF §§2.1–2.3; LA §6.5; compare Term Sheet §3.2.

**What the documents say:**
- **LA §12.2.** The Agreement renews automatically for successive Renewal Terms "**each equal in length to the Initial Subscription Term**."
- **OF §2.2.** Sets the Initial Subscription Term at **60 months** from a July 1, 2025 Subscription Start Date. Each renewal is therefore **five years**.
- **Notice window.** A non-renewal notice is effective "only if delivered during the thirty (30) day period **ending 180 days before**" expiration.
- **Term Sheet §3.2.** Agreed **12-month** renewals, with a simple 90-day-prior notice.

**Why it matters:**
- **The window is narrow and fixed.** The initial term expires on or about June 30, 2030. The only effective non-renewal window is about **December 2, 2029 to January 1, 2030**, over the holidays. A notice sent early is as ineffective as one sent late.
- **Missing it locks Logith in until mid-2035.** During that renewal term:
  - Draibav can raise fees up to 4% at renewal (LA §6.5);
  - the exclusivity in §3.4 continues to bind; and
  - an exit for cause carries the acceleration risk in §12.5.
- **The Issue 3 lapse shows the risk is real.** The client has already missed one contractual window by four days.
- **No term-sheet protection.** The term sheet's 12-month renewal deal was lost to the integration clause (LA §16.2).

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend §12.2 to provide 12-month renewal terms, consistent with the term sheet. Allow non-renewal notice at any time up to 90 days before expiry, deleting the "only if delivered during" window.
2. Consider adding a termination-for-convenience right, at least for renewal terms.
3. In the meantime, docket the December 2, 2029 – January 1, 2030 window, with reminders starting in mid-2029, in the client's and our systems. Raise it in the post-closing integration checklist so the combined company's contract team owns it.

---

## III. Documents reviewed with no material issues

- **Mutual NDA (April 14, 2025).** A standard mutual NDA covering pre-signing discussions. Its disclosure period ends April 14, 2027. Obligations run three years after that, longer for trade secrets. It does not conflict with the License Agreement and creates no exposure for the matters above. One point to note: Term Sheet §12.2 makes the term sheet terms confidential under the NDA, so sharing the term sheet with Ostrander should be done through counsel, consistent with the NDA's provisions on Representatives.
- **Certificate of Insurance (June 2, 2026).** The coverage meets LA §11.1:
  - CGL of $2M per occurrence (plus a $5M umbrella);
  - Tech E&O of $5M per claim;
  - Cyber of $5M per claim; and
  - statutory workers' compensation.
  All insurers are rated A X or better, above the required A- VII. The certificate confirms 30 days' notice of cancellation, consistent with LA §11.2. Points to note:
  - The E&O and cyber policies are claims-made, expire May 1, 2027, and share a combined form. We should request renewal certificates annually and confirm the two-year tail required by LA §11.1.
  - The certificate confers no rights on Logith (COI §1.1). Logith is not an additional insured, and the License Agreement does not require it to be.

---

## IV. Recommended next steps

1. **This week.** Coordinate with the M&A team on the expected closing date and on whether the merger agreement treats the Draibav consent as a closing condition or a covenant. Confirm Logith's payment and use status after October 31, 2026 (Issue 3).
2. **Approach Draibav with a single Amendment No. 2 package** covering:
   - consent to the Ostrander merger and waiver of §§15.2 and 12.5 (Issue 1);
   - narrowing of §3.4 and an Ostrander carve-out (Issue 2);
   - resolution of the Termination Notice dispute or a fresh exit right (Issue 3);
   - conforming the "Licensee Data" definition and tightening §7.4 (Issue 4);
   - amending §10.4(b) to cover Section 8A (Issue 5); and
   - 12-month renewals with a conventional notice period (Issue 6).
3. **Pull the April–October 2026 SLS availability reports** to check for a new Chronic Failure or Severity 1 termination trigger.
4. **Docket** all SLS termination windows and the 2029 non-renewal window.

Please let me know if you would like me to draft the Amendment No. 2 term list or a client-facing summary.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 18, 2026
**Re:** Logith Auto Auctions, LLC: Issues in the Draibav Systems, Inc. LaneCast License Documents

**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed all seven documents in the folder:

1. Software License Agreement dated June 16, 2025 (the "**LA**")
2. Service Level Schedule (the "**SLS**")
3. Order Form No. LC-2025-0614 (the "**OF**")
4. Amendment No. 1 dated May 29, 2026 (the "**Amendment**")
5. Term Sheet dated May 9, 2025
6. Mutual NDA dated April 14, 2025
7. Draibav's Certificate of Insurance dated June 2, 2026

Two background points govern several of the issues below.

**Order of precedence.** Under LA § 2.3, conflicts are resolved in this order: Amendments, then the Order Form, then the body of the LA, then the SLS. **The Order Form therefore prevails over the body of the LA**, and the Amendment prevails over both.

**Integration.** LA § 16.2 supersedes all prior understandings. In any event, the Term Sheet was non-binding apart from its § 12. Where the executed documents depart from the Term Sheet, the Term Sheet terms are lost unless we renegotiate them.

**The pending merger.** Amendment Recital B records that Logith's parent, **Logith Holdings, Inc.**, signed an **Agreement and Plan of Merger dated April 20, 2026 with Ostrander Remarketing Partners, L.P.** Closing is expected in Q4 2026. Ostrander runs its own auction facilities, so closing has direct consequences under the exclusivity clause (Issue 4).

I identified five issues, listed below in priority order.

| # | Issue | Location | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Chronic Failure termination notice sent after the window closed | SLS § 5.2; Amendment Recital C, § 6 | **High (live dispute)** |
| 2 | Data-breach liability now capped because of the Section 8A renumbering | LA § 10.4(b); Amendment § 3 | **High** |
| 3 | Narrower Order Form definition of "Licensee Data" opens bidder and transaction data to commercialization | OF § 4.1; LA §§ 1.9, 7.4 | **High** |
| 4 | Overbroad exclusivity binding all Affiliates across the US and Canada | LA § 3.4 | **High (closing-sensitive)** |
| 5 | 60-month automatic renewals behind a narrow opt-out window | LA § 12.2; OF § 2.2 | **Medium** |

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: The Chronic Failure Termination Notice Was Four Days Late

**Location:** SLS §§ 5.1–5.2; Amendment Recital C and § 6; LA § 12.4.

**The problem.** A Chronic Failure occurs when Monthly Availability falls below 99.0% in three months within a rolling six-month period. Availability was below that level in three consecutive months:

- January 2026: 98.1%
- February 2026: 97.6%
- March 2026: 98.4%

A Chronic Failure therefore occurred. However, SLS § 5.2 requires notice "within thirty (30) days after the end of the third affected month."

- The third affected month ended March 31, 2026.
- The window therefore closed on **April 30, 2026**.
- Logith's Termination Notice is dated **May 4, 2026**, which is **four days late**.

Draibav disputed the notice by letter dated May 11, 2026. Amendment § 6 reserves both sides' positions, including specifically "whether the Termination Notice was timely."

The notice stated an effective date of October 31, 2026, which has now passed. We need to confirm immediately what the parties have actually done since then:

- whether service is continuing;
- whether Logith is still paying fees; and
- whether transition assistance under LA § 12.7 has started.

**Why it matters.** A termination under SLS § 5.2 is fee-free: no early termination fee and no acceleration. If the notice is ineffective, that exit is unavailable. If Logith then stops performing or stops paying, Draibav could treat that as a material breach and invoke LA § 12.5, which accelerates all remaining Subscription Fees. Fees are $78,000 per month, and roughly 43 months remain in the Initial Subscription Term. That is an exposure of more than $3.3 million.

LA § 16.4 and Amendment § 7.2 (no waiver except in a signed writing) make a waiver argument harder.

**Recommended fix.**

1. Confirm the current operational and payment status right away, and do not let Logith act as though the termination is effective until the position is clear.
2. Preserve Logith's arguments under the § 6 reservation:
   - substantial compliance (four days, where Draibav had full knowledge of the failures from its own monthly reports);
   - Draibav's post-notice conduct; and
   - that SLS § 4.4 preserves termination rights as a remedy for an undisputed service failure.
3. Commercially, use the documented failures, which Draibav admits in Recital C, to negotiate a new fee-free exit right or a fee concession. Any such right should be framed as a fresh termination right with a clear deadline.
4. Calendar all future SLS § 5.2 and § 5.3 windows from the date of each monthly report.

---

### Issue 2: Data-Breach Liability Is Now Capped Because of the Section 8A Renumbering

**Location:** LA §§ 8.1, 8.4–8.7, 10.3, 10.4(b); Amendment §§ 2–3.

**The problem.** LA § 10.3 caps each party's liability at fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim, which is about $936,000. LA § 10.4(b) removes the cap for "a Party's **breach of Section 8**."

As originally signed, Section 8 contained the data-security, SOC 2, breach-notification and incident-response obligations (§§ 8.4–8.7). This was the only route to uncapped data-breach liability, for two reasons:

- § 8.1 excludes Licensee Data from "Confidential Information"; and
- the § 9 indemnity covers only IP infringement.

Amendment § 3 **deletes Sections 8.4 through 8.7** and inserts a **new Section 8A** with stronger standards. The Amendment updates the cross-references in § 8.1 and § 12.8, but **leaves § 10.4(b) unchanged**. Under LA § 2.3 the Amendment ranks first.

The result is that a breach of Draibav's data-security obligations is now a breach of Section 8A, not Section 8, and **falls back under the 12-month-fees cap**.

**Why it matters.** Logith holds bidder and consignor registration data, dealer license information, and payment and title data, which is GLBA-sensitive under LA § 7.5. The Amendment was meant to strengthen data protection. Instead, it has removed the uncapped remedy for exactly the scenario of greatest concern. A significant breach could exceed the cap many times over through notification, credit monitoring, regulatory costs and dealer claims.

This also departs from Term Sheet § 8.2, which excluded "data security obligations" from the cap. Draibav's cyber policy ($5M per claim, per the Certificate of Insurance) shows that coverage exists to back an uncapped or super-capped obligation.

**Recommended fix.** Execute a short Amendment No. 2 that revises § 10.4(b) to read "a Party's breach of Section 8 or Section 8A." Consider also stating expressly that costs reimbursable under § 8A.7 are direct damages and not excluded under § 10.1. This change is consistent with the Amendment's stated purpose (Recital D) and should be easy to justify to Draibav.

### Issue 3: The Order Form's Narrower "Licensee Data" Definition Opens Bidder and Transaction Data to Draibav's Commercial Use

**Location:** OF § 4.1; LA §§ 1.9, 2.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.4.

**The problem.** LA § 1.9 defines "Licensee Data" broadly. It covers all data submitted to, collected by or generated by the Platform in connection with Logith's auctions, expressly including:

- bidder and consignor registration data;
- bid histories;
- hammer, floor and reserve prices;
- condition reports;
- transaction data; and
- identifiable derivatives of any of these.

OF § 4.1 redefines "Licensee Data" as data "**uploaded to the Platform by Licensee's Authorized Users**." Because **the Order Form prevails over the body of the LA** (LA § 2.3), the narrow definition controls.

That matters because of who generates most auction data. Bidders and Consignors are not Authorized Users (LA § 1.2). Data they enter, and data the Platform generates (bids, hammer prices, if-sale outcomes), therefore falls outside "Licensee Data."

LA § 7.4 lets Draibav "collect, use, aggregate, analyze and **commercialize**" data "**other than Licensee Data**," including to "develop and sell analytics products, market reports and **market pricing benchmarks** to third parties."

**Why it matters.** Under the controlling definition:

- Logith's ownership right (§ 7.1) shrinks;
- the use limits (§ 7.2) shrink;
- the return and deletion rights (§ 7.3) shrink; and
- the Section 8A security obligations, which protect only "Licensee Data," shrink as well.

Draibav could sell pricing benchmarks built from Logith's bid and hammer-price data to competing auctions. That is commercially sensitive data and the core of the business. It also directly contradicts Term Sheet § 7, under which Logith owns all such data and Draibav may use only non-identifying operational data.

**Recommended fix.**

1. Amend the Order Form to delete § 4.1, or to conform it expressly to LA § 1.9.
2. Revise § 7.4 to limit Draibav's use to aggregated, de-identified operational and performance data that does not identify Logith, any Licensed Site, any Bidder or any Consignor, and that is never used for pricing benchmarks.
3. Ask Draibav to confirm in writing whether it has used or sold any Logith-derived data to date.

### Issue 4: The Exclusivity Clause Is Overbroad and Sweeps In All Affiliates Across the US and Canada

**Location:** LA § 3.4; LA § 1.1 (definition of "Affiliate"); Term Sheet § 4.

**The problem.** LA § 3.4 requires Logith to cause **all of its Affiliates** not to license, use, develop or procure any online, simulcast or mobile vehicle auction software, bidding software or **condition reporting software** other than the Platform. The restriction applies **anywhere in the United States or Canada** and covers both third-party and internally developed software.

Term Sheet § 4 limited exclusivity to **simulcast bidding software at the six Licensed Sites only**. It also expressly preserved Logith's and its affiliates' freedom for all other software and facilities. Because of the integration clause (LA § 16.2), the broader clause controls.

**Why it matters.** "Affiliate" (LA § 1.1) includes entities under common control. Once the Logith Holdings–Ostrander merger closes, expected this quarter, Ostrander and its existing auction facilities become Affiliates of Logith. Their incumbent simulcast, online auction and condition-reporting systems would then put Logith in breach of § 3.4.

The clause also bars Logith from developing its own tools or adopting a competing product at any new site, and the restriction lasts for the full Term, including renewals (see Issue 5).

**Recommended fix.**

1. Before closing, negotiate an amendment restricting § 3.4 to simulcast bidding software used at the six Licensed Sites, matching Term Sheet § 4.
2. Expressly carve out Logith's parent and any entity that becomes an Affiliate through acquisition, merger or investment, naming Ostrander and its subsidiaries.
3. If Draibav resists, at minimum obtain a written waiver of § 3.4 for Ostrander's existing operations.
4. Flag this to deal counsel on the merger so it can be reflected in the disclosure schedules.

### Issue 5: 60-Month Automatic Renewals Behind a Narrow Opt-Out Window

**Location:** LA § 12.2; OF §§ 2.1–2.3; Term Sheet § 3.2.

**The problem.** The two provisions combine as follows:

- **OF § 2.2:** the Initial Subscription Term is 60 months from July 1, 2025, so it expires around June 30, 2030.
- **LA § 12.2:** the agreement renews automatically for successive Renewal Terms "**each equal in length to the Initial Subscription Term**," which means further 60-month terms.
- **LA § 12.2:** non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered during the 30-day period **ending 180 days before** expiry. For the initial term, that is roughly early December 2029 through January 1, 2030. We should confirm the exact dates against the notice rules in § 16.1.

Term Sheet § 3.2 provided for **12-month renewals** with notice at any time up to 90 days before the end of the term.

**Why it matters.** If Logith misses a single 30-day window, it is locked into another five years at $78,000 per month or more, plus up to 4% increases under § 6.5. That is roughly $4.7 million or more per renewal. Exiting early would expose Logith to acceleration risk (§ 12.5).

The long renewal term also extends the § 3.4 exclusivity (Issue 4). Notice delivered too early is as ineffective as notice delivered too late.

**Recommended fix.**

1. Renegotiate § 12.2 to provide 12-month Renewal Terms, as in the Term Sheet, terminable by notice at any time up to 90 days before expiry.
2. In the meantime, docket the non-renewal window now, with reminders well in advance. Add a recurring calendar entry for each future term.
